title: EXION: Exploiting Inter-and Intra-Iteration Output Sparsity for Diffusion Models
problem: Diffusion model inference requires up to 1000 denoising iterations through transformer blocks (dominant 38-100% of operations), resulting in excessive energy consumption and latency; existing transformer accelerators target only QKV projection and attention computation within a single iteration and do not exploit the iterative structure or the dominant FFN layer overhead.
motivation: Diffusion models are 23.6x more energy-hungry and 9.8x slower than GANs for equivalent image quality on identical GPUs, driven by repeated transformer block execution across hundreds of iterations; the FFN layers within each block account for up to 67% of per-iteration operations and are unaddressed by prior accelerators.
method: EXION is a SW-HW co-designed diffusion accelerator exploiting two types of output sparsity. First, the FFN-Reuse algorithm identifies temporal data redundancy across iterations in FFN GELU outputs: one dense iteration is computed fully, then N sparse iterations reuse the GELU output for low-magnitude elements (achieving 70-97% sparsity in the 1st FFN layer, reducing FFN ops by 52-85%). Second, an improved eager prediction algorithm using two-step leading-one detection (TS-LOD) predicts attention scores via log-domain approximation to identify and skip negligible attention computation within each iteration (20-95% intra-iteration sparsity, skipping avg. 26% Q and 22% KV projections). The ConMerge data compaction mechanism converts resulting unstructured sparse output matrices into compact dense forms via column condensing (removing all-zero columns) and block merging (merging sparse and dense tiled blocks using conflict-vector tracking). The dedicated hardware Diffusion-Sparsity Aware Core (DSC) contains: a Sparse-Dense Unified Engine (SDUE) with a 16x16 DPU array with per-DPU input/weight/conflict-vector switches enabling flexible ConMerge-aware dataflow; a ConMerge Assistant Unit (CAU) with sparsity-level sorting and ConMerge vector generation; an Eager Prediction Engine (EPRE) with TS-LOD-enhanced log-domain DPU array; and a Configurable SIMD Engine (CFSE) for special functions. Synthesized at 14nm, 800MHz, 0.8V.
key_novelty: FFN-Reuse: the first algorithm exploiting temporal data redundancy in FFN GELU outputs across diffusion iteration steps to create inter-iteration output sparsity, combined with a ConMerge hardware mechanism that converts unstructured output sparsity into compact matrices executable at high utilization.
contributions: FFN-Reuse algorithm exploiting inter-iteration temporal redundancy in FFN layers, achieving 70-97% output sparsity and 52-85% FFN operation reduction across 7 diverse diffusion model benchmarks without retraining.
Improved eager prediction with two-step leading-one detection (TS-LOD) enabling accurate intra-iteration output sparsity (20-95%) in attention computation for diffusion models without accuracy loss.

ConMerge data compaction mechanism (condensing + merging with conflict-vector tracking) converting unstructured output sparsity into compact dense matrices, reducing remaining columns from 77.4% to 8.4% for Stable Diffusion.

Dedicated EXION ASIC (14nm, 800MHz) with Sparse-Dense Unified Engine achieving 3.2-379.3x speedup and 45.1-3067.6x energy efficiency over a server GPU (RTX 6000 Ada), and 42.6-1090.9x speedup and 196.9-4668.2x energy efficiency over an edge GPU (Jetson Orin Nano) across 7 diffusion model workloads.

metrics.speedup: 3.2-379.3x over RTX 6000 Ada (server GPU); 42.6-1090.9x over Jetson Orin Nano (edge GPU); 5.2x vs Cambricon-D on DiT
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 45.1-3067.6x energy efficiency over server GPU; 196.9-4668.2x over edge GPU
metrics.area: EXION24 (24 DSCs + 64MB GSC): 152.28mm2 vs. RTX 6000 Ada 609mm2
metrics.accuracy: Negligible accuracy loss across 7 models (FFN-Reuse: zero accuracy impact; EP+TS-LOD: minimal PSNR/FID degradation)
metrics.other: FFN-Reuse: 52-85% FFN op reduction; ConMerge: 77.4%->8.4% remaining cols (Stable Diffusion); CAU area: 0.94% of DSC

limitations: ResBlock-containing models (Make-an-Audio, Stable Diffusion) show reduced efficiency gains because sparsity optimizations are only applied to transformer blocks, not ResBlocks; the method does not address non-transformer architectural components.
primary_theme: Inter- and intra-iteration output sparsity exploitation for diffusion model acceleration via FFN-Reuse and ConMerge
